proposed_fix.description: Investigate where inbound request time to emailservice is being spent (network path, sidecar/proxy, CPU throttling, queuing) and apply only gated, reversible mitigations after confirming a cause.
steps: Compare emailservice pod CPU throttling, CPU requests/limits and node CPU/memory pressure against the onset time of the latency rise (read-only check).

Inspect the network path and any sidecar/proxy in front of emailservice for added delay or queuing; check for injected latency (e.g. a fault-injection or network-delay rule) on emailservice pods (read-only check).
If an injected delay rule or recent config change is found, revert it after human approval.
If CPU throttling is confirmed, raise emailservice CPU limit/requests or add a replica, with approval, one change at a time.
Watch emailservice_latency-50/90 and checkoutservice latency for recovery after each change.
preconditions: Confirm the latency onset time in emailservice_latency-90 and whether it correlates with a deploy, config change, or fault injection.
Confirm checkoutservice's elevated latency (E1) is downstream of emailservice calls and not an independent issue.
Obtain on-call approval before any change to resource limits, replicas, or network rules.
proposed_fix.rollback: Restore the previous CPU limits/requests and replica count, and re-apply any removed network or delay configuration from its saved prior state; all changes are made one at a time so each can be undone independently.
